column1: # cpe-extra.csv — component identity that Buildroot's own metadata does not give us.
# Read by scripts/compliance/cve-check.py. Three kinds of row:
#   1. CPE declared      — a cpe:2.3 string for a component Buildroot has no CPE_ID for,
#                          so it gets checked instead of counted as an unchecked gap.
#   2. CPE=NONE          — the component genuinely has no NVD presence. NOTES must say
#                          why, and how its vulnerabilities are found instead.
#   3. component added    — a COMPONENT name that is not in the Buildroot package list is
#                          ADDED to the inventory. That is how the kernel, U-Boot and the
#                          Rockchip SDK get checked at all: they are in the image but are
# MODE: gate (default — findings can block a release) or report-only (counted and listed,
#       never blocking; for components whose fix is a version rebase, not per-CVE triage).
# A wrong CPE is worse than a missing one: it reports a component as clean instead of
# reporting it as unchecked. Verify against the NVD CPE dictionary before adding a row

column6: Rockchip RV1106 vendor kernel (sysdrv/source/kernel), not a Buildroot package. 5.10.160 matches ~5100 NVD records, the overwhelming majority in subsystems and drivers this SoC configuration does not build. Remediation is to move the vendor base to a newer 5.10.y stable, so it is tracked as a version-currency task rather than 5100 individual dispositions; see the OpenSSL/kernel currency item in media/joral/cra-compliance-plan.md.

Rockchip vendor U-Boot (sysdrv/source/uboot), not a Buildroot package. Same remediation model as the kernel — the vendor fork cannot be bumped independently of the SoC support. Reachability matters here: U-Boot is not network-facing in this product (no netboot, no USB mass-storage boot path enabled), so its findings are not release-blocking on their own.

Closed-source Rockchip media/ISP/NPU libraries shipped as binaries (librkaiq, rockit, librknnmrt). No NVD CPE exists for them, so nothing can be queried; vulnerabilities in them reach us only through Rockchip release notes or our own testing. Recorded here so the gap is on the record rather than absent from the inventory.
Buildroot declares no CPE_ID for this package; vendor/product verified against the NVD CPE dictionary (cpe:2.3:a:netfilter:libnftnl).
First-party daemon — no NVD presence by definition. Vulnerabilities are found by our own testing (make test, hardware bench TC-S* cases) and by reports to security@joralllc.com per SECURITY.md.
First-party React SPA + CGI shell scripts. Same as above. Note that its npm build-time dependency tree is NOT covered by this gate and is not shipped in the image (only the built bundle is).

Vendored third-party library (media/joral/eipscanner submodule), statically linked into the daemon. No NVD CPE dictionary entry exists for it, so it cannot be queried; monitored by watching the upstream repository. It parses EtherNet/IP from the network, so it is the highest-value target in this list for our own fuzzing under Annex I Part II periodic testing.
Rockchip closed-source NPU runtime — no CPE. Optional at build time (-DHAVE_RKNN); the float reference path runs without it.
Vendored vendor header, no code shipped from it beyond what the daemon compiles against. No CPE.
First-party daemon — no NVD presence. Found by our own testing and by reports to security@joralllc.com.
First-party console (static HTML/JS + CGI shell scripts) — no NVD presence.
